adds.title: Saint Lucia Domestic Violence Act - passed 8 March 2022
adds.summary: On 8 March 2022 Saint Lucia's Parliament passed the Domestic Violence Act 2022 expanding protection to same-sex relationships via gender-neutral definitions of spouse, cohabitant, visiting relationship, domestic relationship, applicant and respondent, defining domestic violence to include economic and sexual abuse, harassment, cyber-stalking, coercion, threats and intimidation, and requiring under Clause 5 that public officers and service providers not discriminate on grounds including sex, gender, sexual orientation and gender identity, giving transgender victims/survivors equal access to remedies including court protection orders.

adds.title: United and Strong - 2014 human rights sensitisation training and May 2015 follow-up initiative
adds.summary: In 2014 the Royal Saint Lucia Police Force from Commissioner to new recruits underwent LGBTI human rights sensitisation, followed May 19-22, 2015 by sensitisation for Air and Sea Ports, Customs and Corrections officers and interfacing civil society facilitated by Maurice Tomlinson and Tom Decker in partnership with the Canadian HIV/AIDS Legal Network, AIDS Healthcare Foundation, British High Commission, CariFLAGS and RSLPF, ending with training-of-trainers and certificates at the Police Training School in La Toc on May 22, 2015 to sustain more humane professional policing and reduce stigma and discrimination.
